chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadalah, from Jamil ibn Darrāj, from Aban, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi 'Uqbah, from Humran, from one of the two عليهما السلام, who said:

My father used to perform salat (prayer) on the khumrah; he would place it on the carpet and perform sajdah upon it. When there was no khumrah, he would place pebbles on the carpet where he would perform sajdah.

key_terms.الطَّنْفِسَةِ: a carpet or rug upon which the khumrah or pebbles were placed
key_terms.الْخُمْرَةِ: a small mat or woven piece used for sajdah
key_terms.حَصًى: small pebbles used as the surface for sajdah

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to perform sajdah on a khumrah or pebbles placed over a carpet during salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith describes the practice of an Imam عليه السلام in performing sajdah during salat (prayer) upon a khumrah, or otherwise upon pebbles placed over a carpeted surface. It indicates a practical ruling concerning the place of sajdah and distinguishes the material of prostration from the rest of the body's contact in prayer.
